question: A single cell may constitute a whole organism in all of the following, EXCEPT:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rhizopus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rhizopus** is a genus of fungi, also known as bread molds, which are multicellular organisms.
 
• Unlike single-celled organisms, Rhizopus consists of multiple hyphae that form a complex mycelium structure.
 
• The lifecycle of Rhizopus involves both asexual and sexual reproduction, indicating its multicellular nature.
 
• Rhizopus species are primarily saprophytic, growing on decaying organic matter, and do not exist as single cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bacteria**

 
 
• Bacteria are unicellular microorganisms that lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
 
• They reproduce primarily through binary fission, a form of asexual reproduction.
 
• Bacteria can exist independently as single cells.
 
 
 
• **Chlamydomonas**
 
 
• Chlamydomonas is a genus of green algae which are single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• They are known for their two flagella and are often found in freshwater environments.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba**
 
 
• Amoeba refers to a group of single-celled organisms that move and feed using pseudopodia.
 
• They are a type of protist and can live in various environments, including soil and water.
 
 
 
• **Single-celled organisms**
 
 
• Single-celled organisms are also known as unicellular organisms.
 
• They include bacteria, archaea, protozoa, single-celled algae, and single-celled fungi.
 
• These organisms perform all necessary functions within one cell.
